chunks: Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) used to say: 'Whatever dullness afflicts the animals, they are not left ignorant of four things: their recognition of the Lord, their recognition of death, their recognition of the female from the male, and their recognition of the pasture from the fertile land.'

key_terms.الرَّبّ: The Lord (al-Rabb) — the Sustainer and Master; the Creator who governs all creation
key_terms.الْبَهَائِمُ: Animals/beasts (singular: بهيمة bahima) — quadrupeds, especially grazing livestock
key_terms.الْخِصْب: Fertile, verdant land — land rich in vegetation suitable for grazing
key_terms.الْمَرْعَى: Pasture, grazing ground — where animals feed
key_terms.مَعْرِفَة: Recognition, innate knowledge, or gnosis — a direct, experiential knowing distinct from abstract learning

ai.seo_question: What four things do animals instinctively know according to Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin), peace be upon him, reflects on an observable truth about animal instinct — that even creatures considered irrational retain four innate forms of knowledge: awareness of a Creator, awareness of death, recognition of gender, and the ability to distinguish good pasture from barren land. This saying was narrated by his close companion Abu Hamza al-Thumali, indicating the Imam's habit of contemplating natural phenomena as signs of divine wisdom. The teaching subtly invites humans to consider whether they too possess — and heed — these four essential forms of awareness that even animals are not deprived of.
